summary: Iteration 4 (Customer Auth + Wishlist + Checkout-Prep) tested end-to-end. PRIORITY #1 blank-web-screen issue was reproduced, root-caused, and FIXED: AuthContext.tsx imported `expo-secure-store` directly, which has NO web implementation (throws 'ExpoSecureStore.default.getValueWithKeyAsync is not a function'); the mount-time useEffect that read it used try/finally (no catch), so the error was an uncaught exception that broke web rendering entirely (matches the reported blank white page / zero root children / no console output). Fixed by switching AuthContext.tsx to the project's own pre-existing platform-safe storage abstraction (src/utils/storage, which already has a correct index.ts (native, SecureStore) / index.web.ts (web, AsyncStorage) split with built-in try/catch) instead of calling expo-secure-store directly. Verified via browser automation: app now renders correctly on web preview, home screen and all navigation work with zero console/page errors. Backend: 13/13 new pytest cases pass (authorize-url native 200 + web correctly rejected 400 per the intentional security fix, guest 401 on /me and /addresses, garbage-token 401, refresh/logout invalid-token handled gracefully with no 500s, existing Shopify catalog/cart endpoints unaffected). Frontend flows verified via Playwright on mobile viewport (375x667) against the live public URL: guest browsing works everywhere (home, categories->collection, product detail, search bar present); wishlist add/remove and Header badge sync (0->1) verified across Product Detail -> Home -> Wishlist screen, and persistence across an in-session page reload was verified directly via localStorage inspection + reload (heart stayed filled, localStorage held the serialized product); profile screen correctly shows the guest sign-in gate with 'Log In'/'Sign Up' both routing through the same passwordless OAuth hook, and on web both immediately show the graceful inline banner 'Sign-in is available in the Now Kart mobile app...' (useShopifySignIn's Platform.OS==='web' short-circuit) with NO crash/raw error, matching the documented native-build-only boundary; /addresses screen shows a clean guest 'Sign in to save addresses' gate; checkout-prep (POST prepare via /checkout/address) correctly calls live Shopify stock validation - tested with 2 different real products and both were correctly flagged with 'Only 0 left of ... please reduce quantity' because this Shopify dev store has quantityAvailable=0 on effectively every variant store-wide (continue-selling-when-out-of-stock, availableForSale=true) - this is a real, reproducible data/logic gap, not a test artifact (see action items). Full OAuth completion (real email/magic-link verification) could not be exercised, as expected/flagged upfront - correctly confirmed as the boundary of automatable testing (native custom-scheme redirect only resolves in a real device build).

minor.issue: _validate_cart_lines() in shopify_integration/service.py flags any line where quantity > quantityAvailable even when availableForSale=true. This Shopify store has quantityAvailable=0 on every product variant checked (store doesn't track granular inventory / continue-selling is on), so EVERY cart with any item is flagged invalid and the happy-path address-selection UI can never be reached with this store's real data. Recommend only enforcing the quantityAvailable cap when Shopify reports the variant's inventory policy as tracked/DENY, or trusting availableForSale as the primary out-of-stock signal.

ui_bugs.issue: load() does an early `if (!cartId) return;` without ever calling setIsLoading(false) first, so navigating to /checkout/address without a cartId query param (e.g. a direct deep link) leaves the screen stuck on the ActivityIndicator forever with no error/timeout. Not reachable via the normal in-app flow (cart.tsx always passes a real cartId), so this is a robustness/edge-case gap rather than a live bug.

react_native_issues.issue: Directly imported and called `expo-secure-store` (native-only, no web support) instead of the project's own src/utils/storage abstraction that already handles the native/web split correctly. The resulting uncaught rejection (try/finally, no catch) broke the entire web preview on every cold mount. Fixed by switching all 5 call sites to storage.secureGet/secureSet/secureRemove.

action_items: HIGH: Revisit checkout stock-validation logic (shopify_integration/service.py _validate_cart_lines) so it doesn't block checkout for every product on stores where inventory isn't tracked per-variant (quantityAvailable=0 but availableForSale=true) - currently the address-selection happy path is unreachable end-to-end against this store's real data.
LOW: Add setIsLoading(false) (or an explicit error state) to the early-return branch in app/checkout/address.tsx's load() when cartId is missing, so a bad/missing deep link doesn't spin forever.
No action needed: web-platform sign-in gating, guest browsing, wishlist, and the auth security fixes (web-authorize-url 400, guest 401s) all verified working as designed.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.tsx bypassed the project's own established storage.ts/storage.web.ts abstraction (used correctly by src/utils/storage's other consumers) in favor of a raw expo-secure-store import - this is exactly the kind of inconsistency the abstraction exists to prevent, and it caused a total web-preview outage. Now fixed to use the shared `storage` singleton consistently.

useShopifySignIn.ts's Platform.OS==='web' short-circuit (returning 'web-unsupported' before ever calling the backend) is a clean, well-documented way to fail fast for an unsupported platform rather than attempting a flow that can never complete - good defensive design.

Backend correctly rejects platform='web' authorize-url requests with 400 and _validate_cart_lines correctly distinguishes 'out of stock' vs 'insufficient quantity' issue messages - the logic itself is sound, it's the interaction with this particular store's inventory-tracking configuration that makes it always-fail in practice (see action items).

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (all guest/wishlist/gating flows verified working; 1 low-priority edge-case bug found+reported, 1 data/logic gap found+reported, full OAuth completion untestable in this environment as expected)

seed_data_creation: None - tested against live Shopify store data (vcq88p-fj.myshopify.com) and the app's own MongoDB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The web-preview blank-screen bug reported by the dev agent was real and has been root-caused + fixed (expo-secure-store has zero web support; AuthContext.tsx now uses the pre-existing src/utils/storage abstraction instead). Web preview is fully functional again - please restart expo if a fresh test session shows any caching weirdness. Auth-completion-dependent flows (address CRUD with a real signed-in Shopify customer) remain untestable without a native build + real email verification, exactly as flagged in the request - do not mark these as failed, they're an environment boundary. The checkout stock-validation gap (every product flagged invalid due to store-wide quantityAvailable=0) blocks visually verifying the address-selection UI end-to-end; if the main agent adjusts the validation logic, re-run the checkout/address flow with an add-to-cart -> cart -> Proceed to Checkout path to confirm the happy-path address list/selection UI renders correctly.
rca_of_issue: Root cause: expo-secure-store (native-only Keychain/Keystore wrapper) has no web implementation; calling any of its methods on web throws 'ExpoSecureStore.default.getValueWithKeyAsync is not a function'. AuthContext.tsx's session-restore effect wrapped this call in try/finally (no catch clause), so the thrown error became an unhandled promise rejection at the React root on every single web mount, which is why it reproduced identically before and after the reporter's own 5 file changes (it's independent of those changes - the auth feature itself, present since this iteration started, was the root cause) and why zero console output/log lines appeared before the crash (the crash happens inside the very first useEffect pass, before most of the app's own logging fires). Mitigation applied: replaced all 5 expo-secure-store call sites in AuthContext.tsx with the project's own storage.secureGet/secureSet/secureRemove (src/utils/storage), which already has a correct AsyncStorage-backed web fallback and never throws. Verified fix via fresh browser automation run: root element now has real children, home-screen testID renders, and all subsequent navigation/wishlist/auth-gate flows work with zero console/page errors.
